editorial: You follow a group of young ravers in 1991 who sign up for a clinical drug trial hoping for quick cash. The sterile clinic feels wrong from the start, and the experimental drug turns their party energy into something dark. The friends try to stick together as strange symptoms spread, mixing body horror with real friendship drama. The cast sells the fear without going over the top, and the slow build makes the later chaos hit harder. It is not perfect; some side characters feel thin, and a few scares repeat. Still, if you like tense medical horror with emotional stakes, this is a strong pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the last surviving friends learn the trial was designed to create a shared infection, not cure anything at all. The clinic staff try to lock them inside, but one friend sacrifices herself to open the exit. The final twist shows the main character escaping into the city while already showing symptoms, meaning the outbreak is just beginning.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tense medical horror with emotional stakes.
